title: A completed-base etale span and varying base map admit a smooth pointed model
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$ be affine schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to T$ be finite type morphisms of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix $s\in S$, put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, and let $B=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ with closed point $b$, using maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\lambda:B\to T$ be a morphism and put $t=\lambda(b)$, $X_B=X\times_SB$, $Y_B=Y\times_{T,\lambda}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $H$ is affine of finite presentation over $B$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $h\in H$ maps to $b$, and $a:H\to X_B$, $c:H\to Y_B$ are étale $B$-morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing residue-field isomorphisms at $h$. Put $x_B=a(h)$ and $y_B=c(h)$. Then there exist an affine scheme $S'$, a smooth morphism $q:S'\to S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], an $S$-morphism $r:B\to S'$, and a morphism $\lambda':S'\to T$ with $\lambda' r=\lambda$. Put $s'=r(b)$, $X'=X\times_SS'$, and $Y'=Y\times_{T,\lambda'}S'$. There exist an affine scheme $H'$ of finite presentation over $S'$, étale $S'$-morphisms $a':H'\to X'$ and $c':H'\to Y'$, and a $B$-isomorphism $e:H'\times_{S'}B\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ intertwining both arrows with their actual base changes to $X_B,Y_B$. If $h'$ is the projection of $e^{-1}(h)$ and $x'=a'(h')$, $y'=c'(h')$, then $h',x',y'$ lie over $s'$, $\lambda'(s')=t$, and the induced maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')\to\kappa(b)$, $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(x_B)$, $\kappa(y')\to\kappa(y_B)$, $\kappa(h')\to\kappa(h)$, $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(h')$, and $\kappa(y')\to\kappa(h')$ are all isomorphisms [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: First verify Noetherianity without treating finite type on schemes as a ring presentation by definition. The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring] applied to $\mathbf Z$ itself, hence is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally Noetherian by the one-member affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Since $S,T$ are locally of finite type over it, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $S,T$ locally Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] to their whole affine opens: $R,D$ are Noetherian. Let $\mathfrak p$ correspond to $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ with its canonical $R$-map; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A$ Noetherian. Write $C=\widehat A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $C$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, smooth-limit paragraph; Noetherian prerequisites: Algebra Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, and Tag 0316, lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian

proof.text: The maps $S,T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ are locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the whole affine source and target gives finite presentations of $R,D$ over $\mathbf Z$. In particular $R$ is generated as a ring by finitely many elements, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring] makes $R$ a G-ring. Its defining assertion in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], at $\mathfrak p$, says exactly that $A\to C$ is regular. Also $R\to A$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular]. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$, the fibre $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is the localization $(R\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}(C/\mathfrak q C)$: send $c\otimes(\bar r/\bar u)$ to $cr/u$, with inverse $c/u\mapsto c\otimes(1/\bar u)$. The tensor relations and the fraction relations show these are inverse ring maps. This fibre is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], since $C$ is Noetherian. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] hold and the canonical map $R\to C$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, smooth-limit paragraph; More on Algebra Tags 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, and 07QI, lemma-regular-composition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-smoothing] to the regular map $R\to C$ between the Noetherian rings just established. It gives a small filtered diagram of smooth $R$-algebras with colimit $C$ and its actual structural maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] reindex this diagram by a nonempty directed set $I$, still with colimit $C$. Denote the resulting algebras by $C_i$, put $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$, and let $p_i:B\to S_i$ be induced by the colimit maps. Each $S_i\to S$ is smooth, as included in the statement of the Popescu node. The transition maps are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. The affine case of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies $B=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $\varprojlim S_i$, compatibly with these $p_i$. All these are maps over $S$, because the ring diagram and its cocone are over $R$.

proof.text: Put $s_i=p_i(b)$. The completion is local and the canonical residue map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(b)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] applied to the Noetherian local ring $A$. For each $i$ it factors as $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(b)$, by functoriality of residue maps [def-weil-residue-field]. The second map is an injective field map and its image contains the image of the composite, which is all of $\kappa(b)$; it is therefore surjective as well. The first map, being the composite of the inverse of the second with the displayed isomorphism, is an isomorphism too. In particular every stage has the residue-field property required by fixed-family pointed descent.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, observation about kappa(s_i); Algebra Tags 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, and 05GI, lemma-radical-completion

proof.text: Each affine $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and its transition maps are affine by step 3. The map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally of finite presentation by step 2. All maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ commute, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], since ring homomorphisms preserve integers. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to $\lambda:B\to T$. Obtain $i_0$ and $\lambda_0:S_{i_0}\to T$ with $\lambda_0p_{i_0}=\lambda$. On the tail $i\ge i_0$ define $\lambda_i=\lambda_0\circ(S_i\to S_{i_0})$. This tail still has limit $B$: a cone on the tail extends to an arbitrary index $k$ by choosing $j\ge k,i_0$ and composing its component at $j$ with $S_j\to S_k$; a common upper bound proves independence and compatibility, and uniqueness follows from the same formula. Thus $\lambda_i p_i=\lambda$ on every stage of the tail, and $\lambda_i(s_i)=\lambda(b)=t$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, factorization of sigma; Limits Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation

proof.text: Since $S,T$ are locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $X\to S$ and $Y\to T$ locally of finite presentation. They are of finite presentation: their affine sources and targets are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so use [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). Put $P_0=X\times_SS_{i_0}$ and $Q_0=Y\times_{T,\lambda_0}S_{i_0}$. They are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and of finite presentation over $S_{i_0}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Their base changes to $B$ are exactly $X_B,Y_B$. Explicitly the comparison maps preserve the projections to $X$ or $Y$ and to $B$; the inverse maps are the corresponding pullback lifts, so their composites are identities by uniqueness [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $j\ge i_0$ the same comparison identifies $(P_0)_{S_j}$ with $X\times_SS_j$ and $(Q_0)_{S_j}$ with $Y\times_{T,\lambda_j}S_j$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, fixed X_i,Y_i and finite-stage span; Limits Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fixed-family-etale-span-descent] to this directed system, $b$, the fixed $P_0,Q_0$, and the given affine finitely presented $H$ with point $h$ and arrows $a,c$. Step 4 verifies the residue-field hypothesis at every stage; step 6 verifies the fixed models and their finite presentation. The two arrows are etale and induce residue-field isomorphisms at $h$ by hypothesis. The cited node yields a single $j\ge i_0$, an affine finitely presented $H_j\to S_j$, etale maps $H_j\to(P_0)_{S_j},(Q_0)_{S_j}$ and a $B$-isomorphism $e:(H_j)_B\to H$ intertwining the actual pullbacks of both arrows. Take $S'=S_j$, $q:S_j\to S$, $r=p_j$, $\lambda'=\lambda_j$, $H'=H_j$. Use the projection-preserving pullback comparisons of step 6 for the targets of $a',c'$; the two pullback equations are preserved because their projections agree, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives equality of the induced maps. Smoothness of $q$ comes from step 3, and $\lambda'r=\lambda$ from step 5.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, finite-stage span; Limits Tags 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, and 07RP, lemma-descend-etale

proof.text: The point $h'$ is the projection of $e^{-1}(h)$ by construction; set $x'=a'(h')$ and $y'=c'(h')$. The point assertions in [lem-trf-fixed-family-etale-span-descent] identify these with the projections of $x_B,y_B$ in the fixed target models, and give the canonical isomorphisms $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(x_B)$, $\kappa(y')\to\kappa(y_B)$ and $\kappa(h')\to\kappa(h)$. That node also gives that $a',c'$ induce residue-field isomorphisms at $h'$. Its point equations show all three points lie over $s'=p_j(b)$. Step 4 gives both isomorphisms in $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')\to\kappa(b)$, and step 5 gives $\lambda'(s')=t$. These are all the claimed comparisons and point equalities.
